gloss: to raise one's head; to look up

definitions.gloss: to raise one's head; to look up; to lift one's face
definitions.explanation: The physical action of raising one's face from a lowered position.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼女|かのじょ}→彼女：01286_kanojo⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦ゆっくり→ゆっくり：00910_yukkuri⟧{顔|かお}を{上|あ}げた。
⟦{名前|なまえ}→名前：02234_namae⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{呼|よ}ばれて→呼ぶ：00766_yobu⟧、{顔|かお}を{上|あ}げた。
examples.english: Hearing my name called, I looked up.

examples.japanese: {本|ほん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{顔|かお}を{上|あ}げる⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{窓|まど}→窓：02254_mado⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{外|そと}→外：00671_soto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦もう→もう：00602_mou⟧⟦{暗|くら}く→暗い：00647_kurai⟧⟦なっていた→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: When I looked up from my book, it had already gotten dark outside the window.

notes:
A common expression describing the physical action of lifting one's face. Frequently used in narrative writing to describe a character's movements, often to convey emotional states — raising one's head can signal attention, confidence, or a change in focus.

USAGE:
- Very common in novels and descriptive writing
- Often used when a character has been reading, looking down, or in a bowed position
- The opposite action is ⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{下|さ}げる→下げる：00807_sageru⟧ or ⟦うつむく→うつむく：07383_utsumuku⟧ (to look down)
- Can also have a figurative sense: to be able to show one's face proudly

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦ゆっくり→ゆっくり：00910_yukkuri⟧{顔|かお}を{上|あ}げる: to slowly raise one's head
- ⟦ふと→ふと：00048_futo⟧{顔|かお}を{上|あ}げる: to casually look up
- {本|ほん}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{顔|かお}を{上|あ}げる: to look up from a book
- ⟦はっと→はっと：05358_hatto⟧{顔|かお}を{上|あ}げる: to look up with a start

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{見上|みあ}げる→見上げる：04567_miageru⟧: to look up at — focuses on the direction of one's gaze (upward at something)
- ⟦うつむく→うつむく：07383_utsumuku⟧: to look down, hang one's head — the opposite action
- ⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{伏|ふ}せる→伏せる：11515_fuseru⟧: to cast one's eyes down — to lower one's face
- ⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{上|あ}げる→上げる：02443_ageru⟧: to raise one's head — similar but uses ⟦{頭|あたま}→頭：00574_atama⟧ instead of ⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧
